static.topic: Drug Price Control in India: NPPA and DPCO
static.syllabusNode: Government Policies & Interventions — Health; Issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services relating to Health
static.whatIsIt: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) fixes ceiling prices for 'scheduled formulations' listed in the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), and monitors the prices of non-scheduled formulations. Under the current policy, ceiling prices are market-based — derived from the simple average price of all brands of a formulation holding at least 1% market share, with a mandated retailer margin — rather than being cost-plus as under the earlier regime.
static.background: Price control of medicines in India has evolved through successive Drug Price Control Orders issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 — from the cost-based DPCO 1995 to the market-based DPCO 2013. The NPPA was set up in 1997 as the implementing agency. NLEM has been revised periodically, with the most recent list expanding coverage of medicines including oncology drugs. Separately, in 2019 the NPPA capped trade margins on a set of anti-cancer medicines that lay outside the scheduled list, targeting margins in the distribution chain rather than the manufacturer's price.
static.socioEconomic: Cancer care is a major driver of catastrophic health expenditure in India, where a substantial share of total health spending is out-of-pocket. Price ceilings on oncology drugs therefore act as a de facto social protection measure, complementing insurance-based cover.
static.whyInNews: Revised ceiling prices for anti-cancer medicines became effective from Monday, with about 1,000 brands showing a reduction and 203 remaining unchanged, and estimated annual savings of over ₹3,500 crore.
static.wayForward: Widen and periodically update the essential medicines list, strengthen availability monitoring so price cuts translate into actual access rather than shortages, rationalise trade margins across the distribution chain, and pair price control with generic substitution through Jan Aushadhi outlets and quality-assured domestic manufacturing.
prelimsPointers: NPPA functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
DPCO 2013 is issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and uses market-based pricing for scheduled formulations.
Ceiling price computation considers brands with at least 1% market share of a formulation.
NPPA can also act on non-scheduled formulations under the DPCO's public-interest provisions.
static.mainsAngle: Evaluate whether price ceilings on essential medicines are an effective instrument for improving access and reducing out-of-pocket expenditure, or whether supply-side and availability constraints blunt their impact.

static.topic: Ayushman Bharat, Health Financing and Welfare Delivery
static.syllabusNode: Social Justice — Welfare & Rights; Health
static.whatIsIt: Ayushman Bharat, launched in 2018, has two arms: an insurance-based arm (PM-JAY) providing annual hospitalisation cover per eligible family for secondary and tertiary care, and a primary-care arm of Health and Wellness Centres. It operates alongside a broader welfare architecture that combines rights-based laws with DBT-enabled delivery through the JAM (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile) backbone.
static.background: India's welfare model blends rights-based legislation — MGNREGA (2005), RTE (2009), NFSA (2013) — with direct benefit transfer and digital identification. Ayushman Bharat extended this approach to health, and POSHAN Abhiyaan addresses malnutrition. The design reflects a shift from broad entitlement to targeted, technology-mediated delivery.
static.socioEconomic: Insurance cover addresses the hospitalisation cost of cancer care, while drug price ceilings address the outpatient and maintenance-therapy cost that insurance typically does not cover — the two instruments are complementary rather than substitutes.
static.whyInNews: The reduction in anti-cancer medicine prices lowers the cost of prolonged oncology treatment, reinforcing the affordability objective of publicly financed health cover such as PM-JAY.
static.wayForward: Integrate drug price control with insurance benefit packages, expand coverage of outpatient and day-care chemotherapy, reduce exclusion errors in beneficiary identification, and strengthen primary-level screening so that cancer is detected before it becomes a catastrophic expense.
prelimsPointers: Ayushman Bharat was launched in 2018 and has an insurance arm (PM-JAY) and a primary-care arm (Health and Wellness Centres).
PM-JAY provides annual per-family hospitalisation cover for secondary and tertiary care to eligible beneficiaries.
MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household per year.
Four labour codes consolidate 29 central labour laws.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss how price regulation of medicines and publicly funded health insurance together shape financial protection against catastrophic health expenditure in India.

prelims: Revised ceiling prices for anti-cancer medicines took effect from Monday, with about 1,000 brands reduced and 203 left unchanged.
Estimated annual savings from the revision are over ₹3,500 crore.
Ceiling prices for scheduled formulations are fixed by the NPPA under the DPCO framework issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

stories.mainsQuestion: Price control on essential medicines is often presented as the quickest route to affordable healthcare. Critically examine this claim in the context of recent ceiling price revisions for anti-cancer medicines, and suggest complementary measures to improve access to cancer treatment in India.

stories.headline: Heavy rain floods tents sheltering displaced families in Gaza
stories.summary: Heavy rains in Gaza have inundated the makeshift camps where war-displaced families are living, with the Hamas-run government media office stating that about 70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day of rains. The flooding compounds an already severe humanitarian situation in which a large share of the population depends on temporary shelter, with limited drainage, sanitation and winter-proofing. The reported figures come from an authority that is a party to the conflict, and independent verification of the scale of damage is not available in the report. The episode draws attention to the vulnerability of displaced populations to seasonal weather hazards and to the wider constraints on humanitarian access and relief delivery in conflict zones.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a live illustration of the humanitarian dimension of the West Asia conflict, linking international humanitarian law, UN relief architecture and disaster-response capacity — recurring GS-II (IR) and GS-III (disaster management) themes.

perspectives.take: Wire-style report framing the event as a humanitarian consequence of the war, built mainly on the figure released by the Hamas-run government media office; the attribution is made explicit, so the number should be read as a claim by a party to the conflict rather than independently verified data.

static.topic: United Nations and Multilateral Reform
static.syllabusNode: International Relations — Global Governance and UN Reforms
static.whatIsIt: The UN (1945) has six principal organs; the Security Council has five permanent veto-wielding members (P5) and ten elected members serving two-year terms. India has long sought permanent UNSC membership, arguing from representativeness, population and its record as a founding member and leading troop contributor to peacekeeping.
static.background: The G4 (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan) campaigns for Security Council expansion, while the Intergovernmental Negotiations (IGN) process remains inconclusive. Reform debates intersect with the veto, the African Ezulwini Consensus and the demand for greater geographical representation. In humanitarian crises such as Gaza, UNSC deadlock and the funding and mandate questions around UN relief bodies become central to how far the UN can act.
static.whyInNews: Humanitarian relief in Gaza, the role of UN agencies and continuing questions over UNSC effectiveness keep UN governance and reform debates in the news; India's UNSC permanent-seat claim is a standing GS-II theme.
static.wayForward: Text-based negotiations with clear timelines, bridging proposals on the veto for mass-atrocity situations, and broader support for humanitarian mandates and predictable funding of UN relief agencies.
prelimsPointers: UNSC has 15 members: 5 permanent (China, France, Russia, UK, US) and 10 elected for two-year terms.
ICJ sits at The Hague; UN headquarters is in New York.
UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestine refugees, was established by the UN General Assembly in 1949 and began operations in 1950.
static.mainsAngle: Assess whether the UN Security Council's structure and veto arrangements are compatible with effective protection of civilians in contemporary conflicts.

static.topic: International Humanitarian Law and Protection of Civilians
static.syllabusNode: International Relations — International Humanitarian Law and Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict
static.whatIsIt: International Humanitarian Law (the law of armed conflict) regulates the conduct of hostilities and the treatment of persons not taking part in them. Its core rules include distinction between civilians and combatants, proportionality, military necessity and humanity, and the obligation to allow impartial humanitarian relief to reach civilians in need.
static.background: The modern framework rests on the Hague Conventions (1899, 1907) and the four Geneva Conventions of 1949 with their Additional Protocols of 1977 (and a third Protocol of 2005). The ICRC is the principal guardian of IHL, and serious violations can attract individual criminal responsibility, including before the International Criminal Court established under the Rome Statute (1998, in force 2002). UN Security Council resolutions on the protection of civilians have repeatedly reaffirmed obligations towards displaced persons, the wounded and sick, and humanitarian personnel.
static.socioEconomic: Forced displacement, dependence on humanitarian shelter and services, and the breakdown of water, sanitation and health infrastructure are the typical socio-economic consequences that IHL seeks to mitigate.
static.whyInNews: The flooding of shelters for displaced families in Gaza highlights the exposure of protected persons to weather and infrastructure failure, reinforcing debates on humanitarian access and compliance with IHL.
static.wayForward: Strengthen compliance mechanisms, ensure unimpeded and impartial humanitarian access, protect relief personnel, and universalise the Rome Statute; for India, continue engagement with IHL frameworks while retaining its stated positions on related legal instruments.
prelimsPointers: The Geneva Conventions of 1949 comprise four conventions; the Additional Protocols of 1977 (and 2005) supplement them.
The ICRC is headquartered in Geneva and is distinct from the ICC, which sits at The Hague.
Displaced persons, the wounded and sick, prisoners of war and civilians are protected categories under IHL.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss how far international humanitarian law is able to protect civilians and displaced populations in modern asymmetric conflicts, and suggest practical means of improving compliance.

static.topic: Disaster Management, Floods and Humanitarian Shelter
static.syllabusNode: Disaster Management — Disaster Risk Reduction, Flood Preparedness and Relief Logistics
static.whatIsIt: Disaster risk reduction seeks to reduce exposure and vulnerability to hazards such as floods through structural measures (drainage, embankments) and non-structural measures (early warning, land-use planning, contingency shelter and relief planning).
static.background: The global framework is the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, which succeeded the Hyogo Framework (2005–2015) and sets four priorities for action and seven global targets. In India, the Disaster Management Act, 2005 created the NDMA, SDMAs and DDMAs, with the NDRF for response. Humanitarian shelter and relief in conflict settings is coordinated separately through cluster arrangements led by UN and partner agencies.
static.geography: The Gaza Strip is a narrow, densely populated Mediterranean coastal territory whose rainfall is concentrated in the cooler months beginning around late October–November; low relief and constrained drainage increase the risk of localised flooding. This contrasts with the Indian monsoon, a seasonal wind reversal that delivers roughly 75% of annual rainfall between June and September, driven by differential heating, the ITCZ shift and the Tibetan Plateau heat pump.
static.socioEconomic: Concentrated displacement into tented sites, damaged water and sanitation networks, and dependence on external relief multiply the socio-economic cost of even ordinary rainfall events.
static.whyInNews: Flooding of tens of thousands of tents in Gaza on the first day of seasonal rains shows how weather hazards interact with conflict-driven displacement to create a compound disaster.
static.wayForward: Integrate shelter and drainage planning into humanitarian contingency plans, pre-position winterisation material before the rainy season, strengthen early warning and site-level drainage, and preserve humanitarian corridors for relief movement.
prelimsPointers: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030 has four priorities for action and seven global targets.
India's Disaster Management Act, 2005 established the NDMA, with SDMAs at state and DDMAs at district level.
The Indian monsoon delivers about 75% of annual rainfall during June–September; El Niño tends to weaken it and La Niña to strengthen it.
static.mainsAngle: Examine how disaster risk reduction frameworks can be adapted to compound emergencies where conflict-driven displacement and extreme weather coincide.

prelims: The Hamas-run government media office stated that about 70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people in Gaza were flooded on the first day of rains — a figure attributed to a party to the conflict.
Seasonal rains in the Gaza Strip fall mainly in the cooler months beginning around late October–November, unlike India's June–September southwest monsoon.
UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestine refugees, was created by a UN General Assembly resolution in 1949 and began operations in 1950.
International humanitarian law rests on the Hague Conventions (1899, 1907), the four Geneva Conventions (1949) and their Additional Protocols (1977, 2005).
stories.mainsQuestion: Protection of civilians and displaced persons in armed conflict is a core obligation under international humanitarian law. In the light of recent humanitarian emergencies in conflict zones, examine the challenges to delivering relief and suggest measures to strengthen compliance with international humanitarian law.

stories.headline: Kashmir militancy graph falls from 6,800 in 1996 to one, report says
stories.summary: A Deccan Herald report traces the long arc of militancy in Jammu & Kashmir, contrasting an estimated 6,800 militants active in 1996 with a figure of just one at present. The report frames this as evidence of a decisive turn away from armed militancy in the Valley over nearly three decades. It situates the shift within the wider story of India's counter-insurgency and internal security management in the region. The numbers are presented as a reported security assessment rather than an official audited count, and the piece does not detail the methodology behind them. Read together, the account is offered as a marker of how the security environment in Kashmir has changed since the peak years of the 1990s.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly relevant to GS-III internal security — evaluation of counter-insurgency outcomes, the AFSPA/disturbed-area framework, and the institutional architecture (MHA, IB, NIA, state police) that underpins it. Also useful for essay and interview preparation on Kashmir.

perspectives.take: Frames the fall from roughly 6,800 militants in 1996 to one today as a long-term turn away from militancy in Kashmir; a national-desk security narrative that leans on the contrast between peak-1990s and present figures.

static.topic: India's Internal Security Architecture
static.syllabusNode: Security — Internal Security
static.whatIsIt: The institutional and legal framework through which India handles terrorism, insurgency, left-wing extremism and cyber/economic security, coordinated principally by the Ministry of Home Affairs with agencies such as the Intelligence Bureau, the National Investigation Agency and state police forces.
static.background: Internal security management evolved from a largely state-police-centric model to a multi-agency structure. The NIA was created in 2008 to investigate terror offences under the NIA Act. The SAMADHAN doctrine guides the counter-left-wing-extremism approach, while AFSPA continues to apply to areas declared 'disturbed'. Cyber security is anchored by CERT-In as the national nodal agency, with NATGRID and Integrated Command and Control Centres supporting intelligence and response.
static.geography: Pan-India, with distinct theatres: the Red Corridor for left-wing extremism, the Northeast and Jammu & Kashmir for insurgency and terrorism, and urban centres for terror and cyber threats.
static.socioEconomic: Counter-insurgency outcomes are closely tied to development delivery, governance legitimacy, youth employment and the perceived fairness of state institutions — the 'development versus security' debate.
static.whyInNews: A Deccan Herald report cites a steep decline in militant numbers in Jammu & Kashmir, from about 6,800 in 1996 to one at present, prompting discussion of what internal security policy achieved in the region.
static.wayForward: Sustain intelligence-led operations while investing in development, grievance redressal and police reform; strengthen federal coordination between central agencies and state police; and build cyber resilience for critical infrastructure.
prelimsPointers: NIA (2008) investigates terror offences under the NIA Act.
CERT-In is the national nodal agency for cyber-incident response.
SAMADHAN is the doctrine guiding India's counter-left-wing-extremism strategy.
static.mainsAngle: Evaluate whether India's internal security response has been primarily kinetic or developmental, and examine the institutional gaps that remain in federal security coordination.

static.topic: AFSPA and the 'Disturbed Area' Framework
static.syllabusNode: Security — Internal Security (AFSPA, disturbed areas)
static.whatIsIt: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act grants special powers to armed forces deployed in areas declared 'disturbed' by the central or state government, including powers of search, arrest and use of force, with legal protection for actions taken in good faith.
static.background: AFSPA has been applied to parts of the Northeast and Jammu & Kashmir as an emergency-era counter-insurgency instrument. Its operation has periodically been reviewed, with areas de-notified as the security situation improved, and it has been the subject of long-standing debate over human rights and accountability.
static.geography: Applied to notified 'disturbed areas' in Jammu & Kashmir and parts of the Northeast.
static.socioEconomic: Critics link the Act to alienation and reduced trust in state institutions; supporters argue it is necessary for force protection in active insurgency theatres.
static.whyInNews: The reported collapse in militant numbers in Jammu & Kashmir renews the debate on whether exceptional legal frameworks remain necessary and how de-escalation should be sequenced.
static.wayForward: Periodic, transparent review of disturbed-area notifications; phased withdrawal calibrated to ground conditions; parallel strengthening of local police capacity and accountability mechanisms.
prelimsPointers: AFSPA applies to areas declared 'disturbed' under the Act.
Disturbed-area declarations are reviewed periodically and can be withdrawn.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss whether exceptional security laws should be time-bound and subject to periodic parliamentary or judicial review in a constitutional democracy.

prelims: A Deccan Herald report cites militant numbers in Jammu & Kashmir falling from about 6,800 in 1996 to one at present.
NIA (2008) investigates terror offences under the NIA Act.
CERT-In is the national nodal agency for cyber-incident response.
SAMADHAN is the doctrine guiding India's counter-left-wing-extremism strategy.
stories.mainsQuestion: The reported decline of militancy in Jammu & Kashmir from thousands in the 1990s to a negligible number today is cited as a counter-insurgency success. Critically examine the security, legal and developmental dimensions of this transition, and assess whether exceptional frameworks such as AFSPA should be revisited.

static.topic: Indian National Congress: Foundation and Evolution
static.syllabusNode: History — Modern India & Freedom Struggle; post-independence political parties
static.whatIsIt: The Indian National Congress, founded in 1885, was the principal vehicle of the national movement and later became a major political party in independent India, remaining one of the poles of national politics.
static.background: Founded in 1885 on A.O. Hume's initiative; its mass phases include the Swadeshi movement (1905), Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience and the Dandi March (1930) and Quit India (1942); the Cabinet Mission (1946) and the Mountbatten Plan led to the Indian Independence Act 1947.
static.socioEconomic: Historically drew on a broad social coalition; internal factionalism and the erosion of the 'catch-all' party model are recurring themes in analyses of its electoral fortunes.
static.whyInNews: Sonia Gandhi, a long-serving former president of the party, gave an interview to The Hindu ahead of the launch of her book, in which she criticised the BJP.
static.wayForward: Debates on inner-party democracy, organisational renewal and the strength of the opposition are central to the health of Indian parliamentary democracy.
prelimsPointers: Indian National Congress was founded by A.O. Hume in 1885.
The Indian Independence Act 1947 created India and Pakistan as dominions.
static.mainsAngle: Nature of mass mobilisation and the role of marginalised voices; colonial legacies in institutions.

static.topic: Constitutional Morality and the 'Idea of India'
static.syllabusNode: Polity — Constitution: features, values and Preamble; political discourse
static.whatIsIt: The phrase 'fabric of India' is commonly used in political discourse to refer to the constitutional values of the Preamble — justice, liberty, equality and fraternity — and to India's plural, secular and democratic character.
static.background: The Preamble was adopted in 1949 and amended in 1976 to add 'socialist' and 'secular'; the Supreme Court has invoked 'constitutional morality' and the basic structure doctrine to protect these values.
static.socioEconomic: India's diversity of language, religion, caste and region makes accommodation and fraternity persistent governance challenges.
static.whyInNews: Sonia Gandhi's remark that the BJP has done 'great damage to the fabric of India' invokes this vocabulary of constitutional values.
static.wayForward: Strengthening deliberative institutions, civil discourse and constitutional literacy.
prelimsPointers: The Preamble was amended by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, which added the words 'socialist' and 'secular'.
The basic structure doctrine was laid down in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).
static.mainsAngle: Examine how the vocabulary of constitutional values shapes political contestation in India.

static.topic: Political Parties: Registration, Regulation and Inner-Party Democracy
static.syllabusNode: Polity — Elections and political parties; Representation of the People Act, 1951
static.whatIsIt: Political parties are registered with the Election Commission under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951; recognised parties receive reserved symbols and other privileges.
static.background: The ECI registers parties and grants recognition on the basis of electoral performance; the Tenth Schedule (added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985) regulates defection by legislators; inner-party democracy is not statutorily mandated.
static.socioEconomic: Party funding, transparency and the concentration of leadership within families are recurring reform debates.
static.whyInNews: The interview, timed with a book launch by a senior opposition leader, highlights the role of party leadership in shaping national political narratives.
static.wayForward: Debate on state funding of elections, transparency in party finances and internal party democracy.
prelimsPointers: Political parties are registered under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
The Tenth Schedule deals with disqualification of legislators on grounds of defection.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss whether statutory regulation of inner-party democracy would strengthen Indian democracy.

stories.mainsQuestion: The health of a democracy is often judged by the quality of its political discourse. In this context, examine the role of opposition parties and political rhetoric in sustaining India's constitutional fabric. (250 words / 15 marks)

stories.headline: AI-led selloff jolts global markets; crude slips, fuel steady, E20 row flares
stories.summary: A sharp AI-theme-driven selloff on November 5, 2026 pulled down the Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq, with analysts describing the intensity as more than a routine correction rather than a garden-variety dip. Technical readings suggest US benchmarks may see a short relief bounce after further weakness, while Indian market commentary questions whether the Samvat 2083 rebound can sustain given weak breadth and global risks. In commodities, crude has turned bearish with any recovery expected to be short-lived, even as Middle East tensions persist. Retail fuel prices in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai were largely unchanged on November 8, while government data showed India's oil consumption rising 10% in October to its highest level since March. static.topic: Global equity selloffs and financial-market contagion
static.syllabusNode: Economy — Capital Markets and Financial Stability
static.whatIsIt: A sharp, correlated fall in equity indices across markets, typically triggered by a shock to a dominant investment theme and amplified by index concentration, leverage and automated trading. The AI-theme selloff of 5 November 2026 hit the three main US benchmarks — Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq.
static.background: Major precedents include the 1987 crash, the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, the 2020 pandemic crash and the 2022 technology-led drawdown. Over the past decade, US indices have become unusually concentrated in a handful of mega-cap technology firms, so a shock to that single theme moves the whole index. India transmits such shocks mainly through foreign portfolio flows, sentiment and currency movement.
static.geography: Epicentre in US markets (New York); transmission to India via FPI flows, rupee movement and index sentiment.
static.socioEconomic: Retail exposure through mutual funds and SIPs, wealth effects on consumption, and mark-to-market impact on pension and insurance portfolios.
static.whyInNews: The 5 November 2026 AI-led crash was described as more than a routine correction, with technical analysts expecting only a relief bounce and Indian commentary cautioning on weak market breadth.
static.wayForward: Portfolio diversification, robust circuit-breaker and disclosure frameworks, monitoring of leveraged and concentrated positions, and investor education on theme-driven volatility.
prelimsPointers: Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are the three principal US equity benchmarks.
SEBI is the statutory regulator of Indian securities markets; circuit breakers halt trading at specified index movements.
Foreign portfolio investment is a volatile, 'hot money' component of India's capital flows.
static.mainsAngle: Examine how global equity shocks transmit to India through capital flows and sentiment, and assess whether India's regulatory and macroeconomic buffers are adequate.

static.topic: Ethanol Blending Programme and E20 petrol
static.syllabusNode: Economy — Energy Security; Agriculture — Biofuels and Food-Fuel Linkages
static.whatIsIt: The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme blends ethanol with petrol to cut crude import dependence and support sugarcane farmers. E20 denotes petrol blended with 20% ethanol.
static.background: Ethanol blending began in India in 2003 and was expanded through successive policy revisions, with the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 providing the roadmap. The E20 target was advanced from 2030 to 2025. Ethanol is sourced from sugarcane juice, B-heavy and C-heavy molasses, surplus rice and maize, at administered prices. Concerns raised include food-versus-fuel competition, water use in sugarcane cultivation, and compatibility of older vehicles with higher blends.
static.geography: Sugarcane belt of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka; Karnataka's E20 quality claims are the immediate trigger for the news.
static.socioEconomic: Farmer income and sugar-mill viability on one side; fuel import savings, consumer vehicle concerns and food security on the other.
static.whyInNews: The Centre countered Karnataka's claims on E20 quality, stating that tested samples meet prescribed quality standards.
static.wayForward: Strengthen quality assurance and testing infrastructure, diversify feedstock towards maize and second-generation ethanol, and run consumer awareness and vehicle-compatibility programmes.
prelimsPointers: E20 means petrol blended with 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.
Ethanol for blending is produced from sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses, C-heavy molasses and surplus/damaged food grains.
The National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 set the blending roadmap that was later accelerated.
static.mainsAngle: Evaluate the ethanol blending programme as an energy-security instrument against its implications for food security, water use and vehicle compatibility.

static.topic: Crude oil prices, fuel pricing and India's energy security
static.syllabusNode: Economy — Infrastructure: Energy; External Sector and Inflation
static.whatIsIt: India imports the bulk of its crude requirement, so global crude prices feed directly into retail petrol and diesel prices, inflation, the import bill and the current account deficit. Petrol and diesel prices in India are market-determined, with daily revisions by public sector oil marketing companies.
static.background: Petrol pricing was deregulated in 2010 and diesel in 2014, with daily price revision introduced in 2017. Retail prices carry central excise duty and state VAT. India has built Strategic Petroleum Reserves at Visakhapatnam, Mangalore and Padur to cushion supply shocks. India is among the world's largest crude importers and the third-largest oil consumer.
static.geography: Suppliers concentrated in West Asia/Middle East; major refining clusters in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; SPR sites at Visakhapatnam, Mangalore and Padur.
static.socioEconomic: Fuel prices influence transport costs, headline inflation, the fiscal burden of any subsidy, and household budgets; oil consumption is a proxy for economic activity.
static.whyInNews: Crude turned bearish with recovery seen as short-lived amid Middle East tensions; retail fuel prices stayed unchanged on 8 November; India's oil consumption rose 10% in October to its highest since March.
static.wayForward: Diversify import sources, expand strategic reserves, accelerate ethanol blending, EVs and refinery upgradation, and improve pricing transparency.
prelimsPointers: Petrol and diesel prices in India are market-determined and revised daily by oil marketing companies.
India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves are located at Visakhapatnam, Mangalore and Padur.
India is the third-largest oil consumer in the world and imports the majority of its crude requirement.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss how volatile crude prices affect India's inflation, fiscal position and external sector, and evaluate the adequacy of India's energy security architecture.

stories.headline: Krakow shooting: gunman kills at least five in random Main Square attack
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire on people in Krakow's Main Square on 7 November 2026, with police saying he fired at random passers-by as he drove past the city's central square. Initial police statements reported five people killed and about a dozen injured, while later reporting put the death toll at six and said three further bodies were found at the attacker's home. Details of the sequence of events and the final toll continued to be revised as reporting developed, and no motive has been publicly confirmed. The attack is rare for Poland and has renewed attention on public-space security and gun regulation in Europe.
stories.whyItMatters: It links a live law-and-order event to static themes UPSC tests repeatedly — internal security, arms regulation, and the reach of multilateral and regional security cooperation in Europe.

static.topic: United Nations and Multilateral Reform
static.syllabusNode: International Relations — Global Governance
static.whatIsIt: The United Nations, founded in 1945, is the principal global multilateral body with six principal organs. Its Security Council carries primary responsibility for international peace and security, with five permanent veto-wielding members (P5) and ten elected members serving two-year terms.
static.background: India is a founding member of the UN and among the largest contributors of troops to UN peacekeeping. The G4 — India, Brazil, Germany and Japan — campaigns for permanent Security Council expansion, while the Intergovernmental Negotiations (IGN) process on Council reform remains inconclusive.
static.whyInNews: Public-safety and transnational security shocks such as the Krakow shooting revive debate on how far multilateral and regional bodies can coordinate civilian-protection and security responses.
static.wayForward: Sustain momentum on Security Council reform through the IGN and push for stronger, better-resourced multilateral cooperation on civilian protection and public security.
prelimsPointers: UNSC has 15 members: 5 permanent (with veto) + 10 elected for two-year terms.
The International Court of Justice sits at The Hague; UN headquarters is in New York.
static.mainsAngle: India's claim to permanent UNSC membership rests on representativeness, population and peacekeeping contributions; assess the obstacles, including veto politics and the Ezulwini Consensus.

static.topic: Small arms, gun violence and civilian security
static.syllabusNode: Internal Security — Arms regulation and global security governance
static.whatIsIt: Global governance of small arms and light weapons (SALW) rests mainly on the UN Programme of Action (2001) and the International Tracing Instrument (2005), while the Arms Trade Treaty (2013) seeks to regulate cross-border arms transfers. India has not signed the Arms Trade Treaty.
static.background: The UN Programme of Action to Prevent, Combat and Eradicate the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons was adopted in 2001, followed by the International Tracing Instrument in 2005. The Arms Trade Treaty opened for signature in 2013 and entered into force in 2014, but India is not a party to it.
static.socioEconomic: Mass-casualty shootings in public spaces sharpen demands for tighter licensing, screening and urban policing, and disrupt tourism, retail and everyday public life in affected cities.
static.whyInNews: The Krakow Main Square shooting, in which a gunman fired at random people, has renewed attention to gun regulation and public-space security in Europe.
static.wayForward: Strengthen SALW tracing and stockpile management, expand data-sharing on illicit arms, and pair regulation with public-space security design and mental-health outreach.
prelimsPointers: The UN Programme of Action on SALW dates to 2001; the Arms Trade Treaty opened for signature in 2013 and entered into force in 2014.
SDG 16.1 targets a significant reduction in all forms of violence and related death rates.
static.mainsAngle: Discuss whether global instruments on small arms are adequate to curb mass-casualty gun violence, and examine India's position on the Arms Trade Treaty.

onThisDay.description: Myanmar held general elections in which the National League for Democracy, led by Aung San Suu Kyi, won a majority, but the military deposed the government in February 2021. onThisDay.title: UN Security Council Resolution 1441 on Iraq disarmament

onThisDay.title: Creation of the British Indian Ocean Territory
onThisDay.description: The United Kingdom created the British Indian Ocean Territory by detaching the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius and other islands from Seychelles. The Chagos Islands, including Diego Garcia, were later leased to the US for a military base, and Mauritius continues to claim sovereignty.

onThisDay.title: Typhoon Haiyan strikes the Philippines
